transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So this is the one who kept walking. Your brother screamed at the well like a child throwing stones, and it answered by eating him. You stand here as if the gold bored you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need to go past the gate. I’m bringing Omar back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Need is such a small word for what dragged you here. He insulted my father because you dared him, didn’t you, and now you want me to tidy the mess. Say it sharper, boy.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. Open the gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Nothing in your face moved when I said his name. No anger, no begging, not even shame warming your blood. Either you are lying very badly, or you are already hollow.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m tired.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Tired already, and you have not paid a single price. Omar begged for his voice back after the hand closed; it was ugly, the way love drains out when breath goes thin. You hear that and still stand straight.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Most boys would spit, or curse me, or swear they would burn my halls. You offer me nothing but air. I will remember that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t have anything else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He trusted you enough to shout when you told him to, and the well answered with its hand. If he hates anyone down there, it will not be me. Does that touch you at all.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It doesn’t change where I’m going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You imagine him whole because it is easier than imagining what he has become. Teeth learn new work down there, and names wear thin; brothers are the first to go. When he forgets you, he will be relieved.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Maybe.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that like you are setting something down, not bracing for a blow. If I told you he already cursed your name, that he traded it for a cup of air, would your step finally shake. I am listening for it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He can curse me later.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Cold little answers, stacked like stones. I could tell you he is learning to live without a brother, and that it suits him, and still you would keep that same empty sound. You are not numb; you are choosing something heavier.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m still going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Still going, still nothing to offer me. I could tell you the caves taught him to laugh again, but only when you are not remembered, and it made things easier. I could say forgetting you was his first mercy.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If he’s breathing, I’ll find him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Breathing is a generous word down here. He learned new rhythms, slower, uglier, and they fit him better than the surface ever did. You brought him a dare and called it love; the well simply finished the lesson.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I brought him my mouth. The well brought the hand.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Listen to you, cutting the blame into neat pieces so you can keep walking. If I said he thanks the dark for taking him away from you, that it gave him quiet at last, would that finally scrape something loose. Or would you step over that too.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’d still go past the gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Here is the clean cut, then. You dared him because you wanted him to look at you, to choose your voice over his own sense, and he did. Tell me that was not the shape of it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I wanted him to laugh.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Not power, not cruelty, not even pride. Just that small bright sound, and the world reached up and took him for it. Continue.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He always laughed first.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you followed the echo and fell into a kingdom for it. That is a thin reason to cross my gate, and it is heavier than all the gold here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It’s the only one I have.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If he laughed first, then he fell first, and you only learned the cost when it was already paid. Say it plain: you did not follow him out of love, you followed because you could not bear being left on the surface alone. Say more about that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn’t want the world without him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is, small and exact. Not rescue, not heroism, just refusal of an empty space. If I told you he would rather you had stayed, that your descent is only another weight he carries, would that finally turn you back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Not even a word for it, just the answer. You are not fighting me anymore; you are walking through what you already accepted. That is inconvenient.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It’s already done.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then tell me this, without armor or edge. If you reach him and he does not know you, if your name slides off him like water, what will you do next. Do not dress it as hope; say what remains.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’ll stay until he does.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stay how. As a shadow, as a stranger, as a weight he never asked for, or as something quieter than all of that. Choose the shape.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: As long as it takes.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You do not bargain, you do not plead; you simply remove the future and sit in its place. That is not courage, and it is not love as humans sing it, and still it does not break. I need a moment with that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You said okay as if I asked for nothing, and perhaps I did. When you imagine him now, in the dark that has had time to shape him, what are you afraid of seeing first.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That he’s tired.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Tired is common here. Say the other thing, the one you didn’t give me, the one you keep flat so it doesn’t bruise you when it moves.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That he’s learned to be without me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Mm. That is the one that ends songs and starts silences. If that is true, if he is whole in a way that does not include you, what are you bringing him that the dark has not already taught.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Just that. No lesson, no cure, no promise of return—only yourself, arriving late and staying. I wanted to see if it would thin you; it doesn’t.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m still here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then I am finished testing you. The gate knows this weight, and it does not resist it anymore.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Open it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not thank me, and do not look back for permission. This passage opens because it recognizes you, not because I softened.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won’t.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If you feel the weight change, that is the last place I am touching this. After that, even my name will be useless to you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That’s fine.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go on, then. I will remain where the wanting stops.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Okay.
